title: C4044 — Left rear damper solenoid connector
introduction:
I use this reference as an electrical address card for the left rear damper solenoid: the identity table names the connection, the drawing labels its cavities, and the pin table connects those labels to circuits. Keeping those pieces together saves a surprisingly easy garage mix-up—recognizing the housing while reading the wrong wire’s details.

Start by matching the connector description and harness identification. Then match a cavity label in the drawing to the Cavity column and read across that row. Use the service-parts table to cross-reference the listed pigtail and shell identifiers.

This page supports identification and circuit reading. It provides no physical access, probing, electrical-test or replacement procedure. The physical viewing direction, gauge convention and meanings of the Box, Cols, Size and Used entries are unspecified; treat those entries as reference data rather than dimensions or test instructions.

edits.why: I use the cavity labels to connect the illustration to the pin-assignment rows. As drawn, the cavities sit vertically and the housing’s side projection extends left, giving useful landmarks for reading this image. Those landmarks describe the drawing; identifying the physical viewing side requires additional information. The table beneath it associates the illustrated connector with its Fpn and Harness Id.

Start at Cavity and read straight across the same row to connect the circuit identifier, color code, gauge entry, function and terminal part number. That row is the wire’s address—jumping between rows sends the details to the wrong doorstep. The Function entries distinguish the positive and negative sides of the controller-to-solenoid connection. Keep those signs attached to their respective rows; they alone establish neither a chassis-ground connection nor a direct-battery test. A blank Qualifier cell adds no further condition to the entry.

I match Kit List in the identity table to Number here, then compare Hard Shell with Engineering Shell and the connector’s Fpn entry. This ties the pigtail listing to the housing identification. Service Part identifies the listed pigtail service item, while Terminal Part Number in the pin table identifies the terminal associated with each cavity. Keeping those identifiers separate makes the parts reference useful without mistaking a terminal listing for a complete pigtail. The Image entry names a reference file; the attached illustration is the connector cavity drawing.
